title: Make gradient sign consistent
body:
This was meant to follow *shortly* after one of the previous changes so as not to risk inconsistencies.

One of the remaining steps for a stable Optimizable API is that the forces should be minus the gradient, which is not always reflected in the code.  But now at least the Optimizable API does the right thing.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
It involves reassuringly few test changes, and gets to where we want to be. The remaining question is whether it breaks anything. In the 3.26 release notes we said of Optimizable

> Please note that the interface is still considered an internal feature and may still change significantly

and most of the changes are to things that inherit Optimizable, so are Fair Game™️

Technically the change to a method of SciPyOptimizer is public API on something other than Optimizable, so should be a shouty BREAKING CHANGE. (Albeit unlikely to affect real users; we should be able to get away without a deprecation period.)
comments.label_reasoning: The comment discusses breaking API changes to public methods and the consistency of the gradient sign interface across Optimizable and related classes, touching on public API contract concerns.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment flags that a change to SciPyOptimizer's method is a public API breaking change and suggests it should be marked as a BREAKING CHANGE, implying documentation or release notes should be updated.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: The `fprime` method has been there since 2009 so in principle someone could have created code using it since well before we warned about Optimizables.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment raises concern about the long-standing existence of the `fprime` method as public API, highlighting backward compatibility and interface stability issues.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment raises a concern that `fprime` has been public API since 2009, implying that the breaking change may have broader impact than assumed and warrants consideration of a deprecation period or further action.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: @ajjackson is this all right in your opinion?  Any comments?

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: I think that change is not breaking.  SciPyOptimizer, like all optimizers, uses the Optimizable interface and therefore is subject to the same sign flip.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: What `fprime()` does is to call `optimizable.get_gradient()`, which now returns minus what it did before. `fprime()` then negates the result and returns that.  Therefore, it returns the same thing as before.  Its caller will need no change.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: I added this to the changelog.  I'll merge it then.  Thanks!
